definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese art of preparing and serving matcha tea.

examples.japanese: {茶道|ちゃどう}を{体験|たいけん}した。
{茶道|ちゃどう}を{習|なら}っている。
{茶道|ちゃどう}には{作法|さほう}がたくさんある。
examples.english: Tea ceremony has many rules of etiquette.

notes:
{茶道|ちゃどう} is the traditional Japanese art of preparing and serving {抹茶|まっちゃ} (powdered green tea). More than just tea-making, it embodies principles of harmony ({和|わ}), respect ({敬|けい}), purity ({清|せい}), and tranquility ({寂|じゃく}).

ALTERNATIVE READING:
{茶道|さどう} is an equally common reading. {裏千家|うらせんけ} uses さどう, while {表千家|おもてせんけ} uses ちゃどう.

KEY VOCABULARY:
- {抹茶|まっちゃ}: matcha (powdered green tea)
- {茶室|ちゃしつ}: tea room
- {茶碗|ちゃわん}: tea bowl
- {作法|さほう}: etiquette, proper form
- お{点前|てまえ}: the procedure of making tea
- {床|とこ}の{間|ま}: alcove (where a scroll and flowers are displayed)

MAJOR SCHOOLS:
- {表千家|おもてせんけ}: Omotesenke
- {裏千家|うらせんけ}: Urasenke (largest school)
- {武者小路千家|むしゃこうじせんけ}: Mushanokōjisenke

{茶道|ちゃどう} is widely taught in schools and cultural centers and is considered one of the essential Japanese cultural arts.
